articles.title: Serve Robotics to deploy its autonomous delivery robots with Grubhub
articles.summary: Serve Robotics announced a partnership with Grubhub to offer autonomous sidewalk robot deliveries in Chicago, Los Angeles, and Alexandria, Va., while also expanding DoorDash-linked service into Washington, D.C., and San Jose. The company also introduced microdepots for faster city rollout, a restaurant-facing countertop device called Beacon, and conversational AI-enabled advertising characters on its robots. Serve reported strong year-over-year revenue growth but also noted lower-than-expected Uber delivery volume and Uber’s exit from its remaining stake.
articles.advisor_relevance: This is a concrete example of physical AI moving from pilots toward broader commercial deployment through major delivery marketplaces. The article highlights potential second-derivative opportunities and constraints around urban robot infrastructure, charging and dispatch sites, restaurant workflow integration, advertising monetization, and labor substitution in last-mile logistics. However, Serve remains early-stage, with small revenue scale and mixed partner momentum, making execution and adoption risk important in advisor conversations.

articles.title: Budget-First Tariff Recommendation (BFTR): A Complete Algorithmic Framework for Telecom Plan Recommendation without Overcharging
articles.summary: The paper proposes Budget-First Tariff Recommendation (BFTR), an algorithmic framework for recommending telecom plans that align final prices with catalog reference prices to avoid overcharging. Tests on a 974-customer dataset inspired by the Nigerian MTN market show several strategies achieving zero surcharge, fast execution times under 10 ms, and low failure rates.
articles.advisor_relevance: This is an early-stage academic framework rather than a confirmed commercial deployment, so direct investment relevance is limited. It is still useful as a signal that telecom operators may increasingly use AI-driven recommendation and pricing systems to improve personalization while addressing governance and consumer-protection concerns.

articles.title: Low-Rank Dynamics-Effective Latent Carriers for Counterfactual Rollout in Learned World Models
articles.summary: The paper studies whether a small, targeted change to a learned world model’s hidden state can redirect its future predictions along a desired counterfactual path. In a controlled two-object collision environment, the authors find that a single rank-4 hidden-state patch can steer a 12-step autonomous rollout for certain velocity edits, while controls suggest the effect is target-specific for that tested setting.
articles.advisor_relevance: This is foundational AI research with limited direct investment relevance today. It may be directionally relevant to future AI systems that require more controllable internal representations for simulation, planning, or robotics, but the work is confined to a small controlled environment and does not indicate near-term commercial deployment.
